newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ahmsa sees coal output up in '98.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ahmsa sees coal output up in '98.

text.p: The opening of coal mine No. 5 of the steel giant Altos Hornos de Mexico will help boost the company's coal mineral volume output for steel use to 5 million tonnes by 1998, a spokesman said Friday.
The new mine, close to the U.S. border in the state of Coahuila, will have an annual output capacity of 2 million tonnes of coal for use downstream in the steel industry, he said.
"In 1996, the output was 4.2 million tonnes, in 1997 it is going to climb to 4.5 million and for 1998 with mine No. 5 it will reach 5 million tonnes," he said.

Mine No. 5, just starting production, will achieve full output capacity in January 1997. It will substitute the company's mine No. 1. Ahmsa announced recently it would close the reserve-depleted mine.

Aside its output of coal used in steel production, Ahmsa is also the country's main thermic coal producer, mining more than 8 million tonnes per year, which is largely sold to the Federal Electricity Commission for power production.
